newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares static in listless early floor trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares static in listless early floor trade.

text.p: German shares treaded water in early bourse trade on Monday, supported on the one hand by the stronger dollar but with dealers sceptical about the viability of further gains on the other.
The DAX index, which measures floor trade in 30 blue-chip German shares, was down 2.77 points, or 0.08 percent, at 3,371.33 points amid poor early volumes.
This was seen as a subdued reaction to the weekend surge of the dollar to 56-month highs against the mark. June DAX futures rose 16.5 points to 3,376.
"There is a high degree of scepticism in the market," said one trader, noting continued concern over a possible U.S.-led credit tightening.

The dollar is now seen rising, in the mid- to longer-term possibly up to 1.80 marks, after a communique from the Group of Seven at the weekend was interpreted as not expressing dissatisfaction with the current high value of the dollar.
Chemical group Hoechst gained 1.60 marks to 67.80 marks on the dollar strength.
Daimler-Benz AG gained earlier on reports of heavy job cuts and a separate British newspaper report of a merger between Airbus and U.S.-based Lockheed.
Daimler-Benz Aerospace is one of four European partners in the Airbus plane-making consortium. London-based equity analysts contacted on Sunday said they were treating the report sceptically.
Daimler, whose shares were up 25 pfennigs at 127.70 marks in early bourse, later denied plans for heavy job cuts, saying it saw its staff levels as stable over the coming years.
Car-maker Volkswagen went ahead in pre-bourse electronic trade, but fell in early bourse to stand at 1,083 marks, down 2.50 marks.
Initial gains were prompted by comments by VW's chairman Ferdinand Piech, who was quoted saying he was aiming to quadruple pre-tax profits by 2000.
Piech was quoted in the "Focus" news magazine as saying the group would save costs by reducing the number of basic structures on which future VW cars would be built.
Dealers said the start of dealings in finance, savings and insurance group BHW Holding later today would probably be one of the day's trading focuses.
BHW said at the weekend it would be pricing its shares at 26 marks each, towards the top of the range set for the bookbuilding process, and that its issue had been 14.5 times oversubscribed.
